clue.text: A vegetable daughter served with European fish

blocks.note: a European from Switzerland
the char is a fish of the trout family
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A restaurant dish: a vegetable side served to a daughter alongside fish from somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the daughter first, but her letter comes last, after the European and the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a leafy green beet grown and eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Gang, following opening of safe, finds wages

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter, so only that is kept
following says the gang's letters come after the other piece rather than before it

blocks.note: first letter of safe
a crew is a gang of workers

explanation.surface: A gang of safecrackers gets the safe open and finds the payroll inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is old British slang for a wage or salary.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British usage a screw is someone's pay, as in earning a good screw.

clue.text: Impressed one northern writer with first of diaries

indicators.note: the first of a word is its initial letter, which is all that is taken from that word

blocks.note: Roman numeral for one
N is the abbreviation for northern
a scribe is one who writes
initial letter of diaries

explanation.surface: Someone was impressed by a writer from the north who started off keeping diaries.
explanation.walkthrough: Impressed is not about admiration here but about pressing marks into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to engrave or stamp letters into something, which is a literal sense of impress.

clue.text: Making fine distinctions in separating fast runners, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the phrase is matched by how it is said, not spelt

blocks.note: hares are fast runners, and splitting them up separates them; said out loud it matches the idiom

explanation.surface: A race judge agonises over the tiny margin separating the leaders at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting hairs is the idiom for arguing over trivially fine differences.

clue.text: Crowd in store, reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is matched on sound

blocks.note: a hoard is a hidden store of valuables

explanation.surface: News of a crush of shoppers packed into a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large, disorderly crowd of people.

clue.text: Self-control shown by all at home in desert

indicators.note: in places the home piece inside the word for one who deserts

blocks.note: the rest means all the others
to rat is to desert or betray one's side
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A tribute to a family who stay calm and composed while stranded at home in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert is a verb here, not sandy land: to rat on a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is the quality of holding oneself back, which is self-control.

clue.text: Hit has friend's backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a pal is a friend; with the 's it gives the plural form

explanation.surface: A boxer's punch lands because a mate is supporting him from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a blow with the open hand, a kind of hit.

clue.text: Slip made by Liberal over recess

indicators.note: in a down clue over means sitting on top of, so the first piece is written above the second

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
an apse is a vaulted recess at the end of a church

explanation.surface: A political gaffe by a Liberal politician during the parliamentary recess.
explanation.walkthrough: Recess suggests a parliamentary holiday, but it is the architectural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a small error or momentary failing, the same as a slip.

clue.text: Urge boss to produce a small fastener

blocks.note: to press someone is to urge them
a boss is a raised knob or stud

explanation.surface: An instruction to lean on the manager to get a minor item made.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss means a raised ornamental knob, not a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A press stud is a two-part snap fastener on clothing, known in America as a snap.

clue.text: A liqueur is sent in error — a cocktail's required

indicators.note: something sent in error has gone wrong, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A barman's mix-up: the wrong liqueur arrived, but a cocktail is what was ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila sunrise is a cocktail of tequila, orange juice and grenadine.

clue.text: One taking Arabs illegally?

blocks.note: surface reading: a kidnapper or people smuggler seizing people from Arabia
setter's reading: Arabs are a breed of horse, and a thief of horses or cattle has a name of his own

explanation.walkthrough: Arab is a breed of horse, so the thief is one who steals livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is someone who steals horses or cattle.

clue.text: Popular novelist includes page identifying tower

indicators.note: includes means one thing holds another inside it

blocks.note: a writer surnamed Steele
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A bestselling author's book has a page that names a particular tower.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist is Steele; the bestseller Danielle Steel spells her name without the final E, so the clue is a little loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall tower and spire of a church.

clue.text: Was the dominant partner dressed in article, an alternative to a kilt?

blocks.note: if you wore it, you were dressed in it
the definite article
legwear a Scot might choose instead of a kilt

explanation.surface: A Scottish husband's choice of clothes: did he go for a kilt or something else?
explanation.definitionFit: To wear the trousers is the idiom for being the one in charge in a relationship.

clue.text: Chatter endlessly with minister

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: to rabbit on is British slang for chattering

explanation.surface: A talkative parishioner goes on and on at the minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit is British informal for talking at length, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and leader, a minister of a congregation.

clue.text: Pay back bruiser becoming upset with me

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Settling a debt with a tough guy who is getting angry with the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to repay money someone has spent or lost.

clue.text: Aquatic bird, catching one, returned to me, a cliff-ledge nester

indicators.note: catching means seizing and holding, so one piece goes inside the other
returned means sent back the way it came, so the words are read backwards

blocks.note: a gull is a seabird
Roman numeral for one
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A seabird catches a fish and brings it back to the speaker before settling on its cliff ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: Aquatic bird looks like the definition, but the definition is at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a seabird of the auk family that breeds in crowded colonies on narrow cliff ledges.

clue.text: Grim-faced handling it at sink

indicators.note: handling means holding in the hands, so one word wraps around the others

blocks.note: grave means serious and grim in expression
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stands at the kitchen sink, scowling as they deal with the washing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sink looks like the kitchen sink, but it is a verb: to fall downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To gravitate is to move or fall down under gravity, so to sink.

clue.text: Girl, so mad about flowers

indicators.note: about means all over the place, so these letters are moved round

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A girl who is crazy about flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Marigolds are orange and yellow garden flowers.

clue.text: Gibe inside pub — worker gets angry

indicators.note: inside places the gibe within the word for a pub

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
a dig is a pointed remark
the worker ant

explanation.surface: A labourer in a pub is taunted and loses his temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant means resentful and angry at unfair treatment.

clue.text: Cut up piece of rug in outhouse

indicators.note: a piece of the word is its first letter only
in places one piece inside the building word

blocks.note: a shed is an outhouse
first letter of rug

explanation.surface: Someone finds a chewed-up scrap of rug in the garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred is to tear or cut into thin strips.

clue.text: In vicarage, lamb's cooked with a marinade

indicators.note: cooked means mixed and prepared, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: letters to rearrange
taken as written, also part of the mix

explanation.surface: Sunday lunch at the vicarage: lamb roasted with a marinade.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsamic vinegar is a dark Italian vinegar often used as a marinade or dressing.

clue.text: Left one brother a sign

blocks.note: L for left
Roman numeral for one
Br is the abbreviation for brother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sibling was left a sign in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Went to the polls opposing old Edward

blocks.note: v for versus, meaning against
O is the abbreviation for old
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone cast a ballot against an old candidate called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to the polls is to cast a ballot in an election.

clue.text: Out of practice? Game's extremely tricky

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters are taken

blocks.note: RU is rugby union, plus the S from the apostrophe
the first and last letters of tricky

explanation.surface: A rusty player finds the match very tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty describes a skill gone stale from lack of use.

clue.text: Girl in dressing gown runs taps without another thought

indicators.note: without means lacking, so some letters are removed

blocks.note: a robe is a dressing gown
R for runs in cricket scoring
taken as written
PS, a postscript, is a thought added after the letter

explanation.surface: A girl in her dressing gown turns on the taps absent-mindedly.
explanation.walkthrough: PS is taken away from taps; a postscript is literally an afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: Roberta is a girl's name.

clue.text: Toys in sacks by end of cot

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: last letter of cot
to rifle is to ransack, so sacks

explanation.surface: Toys stuffed into sacks at the foot of a baby's cot, as at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: Toys and sacks are verbs: toys with means trifles with, and sacks means plunders.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy with it, treating it carelessly.

clue.text: Some weighed a mozzarella cheese

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: runs across the end of weighed, all of a and the start of mozzarella

explanation.surface: At the deli counter, someone weighed a ball of mozzarella.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozzarella looks like the cheese being defined, but the defining word is the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coating.

clue.text: Unnecessarily provokes, knowing

blocks.note: to needle someone is to provoke or irritate them
a sly look is a knowing one

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble pointlessly while fully aware of what they are doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlessly means without any need, which is the same as unnecessarily.
